data.gender_notes: Musbih is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Musbih means Intense or Passionate in Arabic. It is derived from the root 's-b-h' which denotes fervor, ardor and zeal. The name Musbih carries the meaning “Intense, Passionate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Musbih usually hope their child will grow to embody intense, passionate and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Musbih total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In different contexts within Arab and Muslim societies, the term Musbih can be used both appreciatively and critically. Politically, an intense and passionate political activist can be referred to as 'Musbih'. Similarly, in the context of art, a Musbih artist is someone who creates with an intense and passionate emotionality.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islam, being a Musbih is recognized as one of the virtues of a believer. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "And as for the one who was intense in his love for us and meeting us, Allah will be intensely loving towards him in the Hereafter, and will cause him to enter Paradise with a mighty entrance" [Bukhari, Muslim]. Muslims are encouraged to be passionate in their devotion to Allah, and their desire to reach Him, in line with the Hadith mentioned above. Additionally, being Musbih is also seen as an essential quality for a follower of Sufism (Islamic mysticism), requiring ardor and intensity in the love and longing for the Divine.

historical_references.context: Musbih ibn Umair was a prominent Sahabi (companion) of the Prophet Muhammad. He was a member of the Ansar (helpers) of Medina and took part in several battles alongside the Prophet.
